coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 4–5 miles, sub-Z2 effort (140 bpm max), rolling terrain if available. Your resting HR is elevated at 74 bpm (vs. your 30-day avg of 66.5) and recovery score sits at 46/100—you're in moderate fatigue with 24 days to race. This is taper, not maintenance; cut the intensity entirely. The 6.18-mile run at 126 bpm last week did its job. Now we're pruning volume and letting your aerobic base stay sharp without burning matches. 45–50 min total, no watch anxiety.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Get 1.5–2g carbs per kg body weight today (assume ~75–90g if you're 50–60kg; scale up if heavier). Your sleep efficiency is 70%—below ideal—which signals either light sleep or fragmentation; carbs at dinner and a small snack 2 hours before bed will stabilize blood sugar and improve sleep depth. On a taper, fuel is how you recover. Hit protein at each meal (25–30g), especially post-run, to support adaptation without adding volume.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Prioritize sleep *hard* for the next three weeks. You logged 8.3 hours last night but at 70% efficiency—likely due to travel, time zones, or stress from the constant exec grind. Aim for 9 hours tonight in a cool, dark room; blackout curtains and earplugs if you're in a hotel. Twenty-four days out, sleep is a performance drug. Skip the ice bath; focus on 10 min of easy mobility work (hips, calves, ankles) post-run and call it done.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're coming into taper at the right place—fit, not fried. The 46/100 recovery score and elevated RHR aren't alarms; they're signals that hard work happened. Expect some pre-race anxiety over the next 3 weeks; it's normal. Use Tuesday and Wednesday workouts (light today, some tempo or hill work Wednesday if you feel it) to convince your legs they're ready. By week 34, you'll reduce further and lean into confidence, not doubt. The Julian Alps vert is real, but you've logged the work.
